C005.subject: Class size reduction
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Class size reduction educational outcomes in literacy]

[PATH:empirical] Tennessee Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio (STAR) experiment — A landmark randomized controlled trial that directly tests the effect of class size reduction on literacy outcomes in K-3, providing causal evidence within the specified domain and temporal scope.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis by Hattie (2009) on class size effects in literacy — Synthesizes multiple studies to estimate overall effect size and identify moderators (e.g., grade level, socioeconomic status), helping to clarify the disputed status of the hypothesis.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal analysis of California's Class Size Reduction program (CSR) using NAEP data — Quasi-experimental design leveraging state policy variation to assess literacy outcomes over time, addressing geographic specificity (United States) and potential confounds like teacher quality.

C006.subject: Class size reduction
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Class size reduction educational outcomes]

[PATH:empirical] Tennessee Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio (STAR) experiment reanalysis — Re-analyzing this landmark randomized controlled trial with modern causal inference methods could test whether long-term outcomes (e.g., test scores, graduation rates) show worsening effects, especially for subsets of students.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of class size reduction studies (2000-2020) focusing on effect sizes by grade level — A systematic review of quasi-experimental and experimental studies within the specified temporal and geographic scope can quantify the net direction and magnitude of effects, potentially revealing conditions under which class size reduction worsens outcomes.

[PATH:theoretical] Simulation model of resource reallocation under class size reduction policies — Building a model that accounts for trade-offs (e.g., hiring less experienced teachers, reduced per-pupil resources) could explain mechanisms by which class size reduction might lead to worse educational outcomes in early elementary grades.

C007.subject: Targeted teacher training
C007.object: impact of class size reduction on educational outcomes
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Targeted teacher training impact of class size reduction on educational outcomes]

[PATH:empirical] Project STAR (Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio) follow-up studies focusing on secondary math and science outcomes post-2010 — Reanalysis of the randomized class-size reduction experiment, specifically examining whether targeted teacher training moderates long-term effects in U.S. secondary STEM classrooms.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of teacher professional development interventions combined with class size policies (e.g., from the What Works Clearinghouse or Campbell Collaboration) — Synthesizes existing studies to test the interaction effect between targeted training and class size reduction on math/science achievement, controlling for publication bias and study quality.

[PATH:empirical] Quasi-experimental design using state-level panel data (e.g., from NAEP or state longitudinal data systems) comparing districts with and without targeted teacher training programs before/after class size reduction mandates — Leverages natural variation in policy implementation across U.S. states post-2010 to isolate the moderating role of training on class size effects in secondary STEM education.

C008.subject: Class size reduction
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Class size reduction educational outcomes]

[PATH:empirical] Project STAR (Tennessee Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio) long-term follow-up studies focusing on secondary math and science outcomes — Project STAR is a landmark randomized experiment on class size reduction. Re-analyzing its data specifically for secondary mathematics and science achievement (grades 9-12) in the U.S. from 2000-2020 could directly test whether early class size reductions worsen later outcomes in these domains.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of class size effects on secondary STEM achievement, e.g., Hattie's Visible Learning or systematic reviews by the What Works Clearinghouse — A comprehensive meta-analysis synthesizing studies from 2000-2020 in U.S. secondary math/science classrooms can reveal whether the overall effect is negative, as hypothesized, or positive, and identify moderators such as implementation fidelity or student demographics.

[PATH:empirical] State-level administrative data linking class size policies (e.g., California's class size reduction program) to student outcomes in secondary math and science, using quasi-experimental methods like difference-in-differences — Natural experiments from policy changes allow causal inference. Analyzing longitudinal data on secondary math/science test scores before and after class size mandates can confirm whether reductions worsen outcomes, possibly due to teacher quality dilution or resource reallocation.
